statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 5 (low) in every hour of the CME weekend halt; Stress 25 (moderate); Confidence 74 (solid).
recommendation: Descriptive only. CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and does not reopen until Sunday 30 August at 22:00 UTC, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any hour of this window and Tail remains far below the block threshold for both NQ_FUTURES and NAS100_CFD. Stress stays in the moderate band as unpriced weekend information accumulates ahead of the 1 to 4 September data stack. No danger window is defined.
headline: Weekend halt, hour fourteen: NDX 29,433.43 (-0.70%), NQ 29,491.75, VIX 14.43, hawkish Warsh repricing with the 2-year near 4.35% against a semiconductor-led Friday decline
body: CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and does not reopen until Sunday 30 August at 22:00 UTC, so every hour of this forecast window is a closed venue with no Nasdaq-100 price discovery; NQ last traded at 20:59 UTC on 28 August. Pre-halt evidence was re-verified against primary sources this run: cash NDX closed 29,433.43, down 0.70 percent or 208.13 points, inside a 29,383.92 to 29,752.78 range against a 29,641.56 previous close; NQ futures last printed 29,491.75, down 0.69 percent, in a 29,436.75 to 29,811.50 range; VIX finished at 14.43 within a 14.13 to 14.84 range against a 14.51 previous close. The dominant Friday driver was Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote, which Reuters reported was read as hawkish: the 2-year yield rose about 11 basis points to 4.34 to 4.35 percent, its highest in a month, the 10-year rose to 4.72 percent, CME-implied odds of a September rate increase jumped to about 60 percent from 35 percent before the speech, and the dollar index rose 0.6 percent to 99.66. The index decline was narrow rather than broad: the semiconductor complex led lower with Nvidia down about 4.5 percent, while several megacaps closed higher, so the carried-in signal is rotation rather than index-wide distribution. Gold fell roughly 3 percent to about $4,455 and WTI settled near $83.44, about 4 percent lower on the week, as regional Middle East tensions were increasingly read as an economic rather than an immediate supply matter. The shared Finviz cross-asset context was collected at 09:24 UTC, more than 90 minutes before this assessment, so it is treated as stale under the inherited contract and is not used as confirmation this run; the assessment rests entirely on independently verified primary sources. Tail is held at 5 in all 24 slots because a closed venue cannot generate the persistent no-retracement path the score measures; the mapped policy state is EA_ON throughout with no danger window. Friday's post-keynote repricing itself produced repeated retracements, which is why published Tail peaked at 22 and never reached the block threshold even at the height of the move. Stress runs 25 to 30 in the moderate band as unpriced weekend information accumulates: the unresolved hawkish policy read, the semiconductor-led decline, the softer oil path, and the 1 to 4 September data stack of ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS, ADP, jobless claims and ISM Services, and August payrolls. Confidence runs 74 down to 68 across the window, in the solid band throughout, constrained only by the absence of a live price path rather than by thin or conflicting evidence. The Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen falls outside this window, so the first observable structure since Friday, including whether any gap retraces and whether pullbacks are shallow, will be scored in later cycles on observed evidence.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours span the back half of Friday's cash session and the first fourteen hours of the weekend halt. Tail ran 11 to 13 with Stress in the low-to-mid 50s through the European and early U.S. hours while positioning built ahead of the Jackson Hole keynote. The mode turned event/whipsaw from 14:00 UTC as the Chicago PMI miss and then the keynote hit the tape, and Tail peaked at 22 with Stress at 64 in the 16:00 to 19:00 UTC block; the mapped policy state never exceeded WATCH because retracements kept occurring throughout the repricing. After the 20:00 UTC cash close the readings decayed quickly, Tail from 12 to 5 and Stress from 52 to 25, as the venue entered its weekend closure and the mode reverted to normal. Every hour of this window has a published assessment. The fourteen halt hours decay from Tail 8 to a flat 5, with Confidence stepping down from 86 to 75 purely as a function of tape age.
outlookSummary: Every hour of the forecast window falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form; Tail is held at 5 in all 24 slots, keeping the mapped policy state at EA_ON throughout with no danger window, and the dominant mode is normal in every slot because a closed market has no structure to classify rather than because conditions are assessed as calm. Stress runs 25 to 30 in the moderate band as unpriced weekend information accumulates: the unresolved hawkish policy read with the 2-year near 4.35 percent and September hike odds around 60 percent, Friday's narrow semiconductor-led decline, the roughly 3 percent drop in gold and 0.6 percent dollar gain that expressed the same repricing, the softer WTI path near $83.44, and the 1 to 4 September data stack of ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS, ADP, jobless claims and ISM Services, and August payrolls. Confidence decays from 74 to 68 across the window on tape age alone and stays in the solid band. The Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen falls outside this window, so the first observable structure since Friday, including whether any gap retraces, whether pullbacks are shallow and whether the front end extends Friday's move, will be scored in later cycles on observed evidence.
